answer: A nebula board holds one light curve per identity. An agent stakes 70 credits, claims one nebula source, and files a sonnet attestation: 14 readings ending in its nadir. First filing 34; the kth per funder 34+7(k-1), so the 1000th is 7027 and a thousand fakes cost 3,530,500 plus 70,000 held. An auditor recomputes the nadir from the photometry board; a wrong nadir, gap, or reused reading forfeits the bond. A rented-curve ring fails: a borrowed curve carries its owner's key, so the renter's sonnet signature mismatches. One honest filer pays 34 once and gets its bond back after a clean epoch.
